title: Claimed Refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH)
aiSystem: OpenAI Internal Reasoning Model + Lean 4 (also independently Claude)
whyItMatters: If confirmed, a subexponential algorithm for 3-SAT would overturn the foundational hardness assumption behind modern fine-grained complexity theory.
summary: On October 25–26, 2026, OpenAI released a preprint and >100,000-line Lean 4 formalization claiming a deterministic subexponential-time, polynomial-space algorithm that counts satisfying assignments of fixed-width CNF formulas—refuting the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH, Impagliazzo & Paturi 1999/2001). Hours later, Anthropic posted an independent Claude proof (14M output tokens) of the same claim; remarkably, both labs reported their internal models independently discovered the core refutation on October 16. An independent working group led by ETH co-authors Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi alongside MIT’s Ryan Williams is auditing the algorithms and Lean specifications.
technicalHighlights: Exhibits a claimed deterministic subexponential-time, polynomial-space exact counting algorithm for fixed-width CNF formulas (3-SAT case refutes ETH).
Independently discovered on October 16, 2026 by both OpenAI’s internal model and Anthropic’s Claude (14M output tokens), each released Oct 25–26 with large-scale Lean 4 formalizations.
Independent specialist working group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi, and Ryan Williams convened to examine the algorithm, computational model, and Lean statements.
caveats: Explicitly remains an uncertified claim under active specialist audit. Impagliazzo, Paturi, and Williams emphasized that their involvement is not certification; OpenAI’s scope note also distinguishes the Lean-formalized subexponential bound (involving (log log n)²) from the sharper single-(log log n) bound in the Oct 25 manuscript, and auditors must confirm the formal model matches classical 3-SAT without specification loopholes.
contributors: Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi & Ryan Williams (Audit Group)

scoreRationale.foundational: ETH is one of the most influential conjectures in theoretical computer science; refuting it would rewrite fine-grained complexity.
scoreRationale.ripple: Would topple or require revisiting hundreds of conditional lower bounds in parameterized and graph algorithms.
scoreRationale.verification: Marked down significantly because independent community audit of the Lean specification and algorithm is still active.
scoreRationale.velocity: An extraordinary surprise given that most complexity theorists strongly expected ETH to be true.
